what: The UTM Builder adds campaign tracking tags to a web address. When someone clicks the tagged link, your analytics tool records the source, medium and campaign, so you can see which social post, newsletter, ad or printed poster actually brought visitors and sales.

It is made for marketers, small business owners, creators, nonprofits and students running campaigns anywhere in the world. Presets fill in sensible values for popular channels, and a QR code is generated for every link for use on printed material.
The standard utm_ tags work with almost every analytics tool. Links are built in your browser.
uses: Tag links in posts, bios and stories to compare Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn and others.
See how many visitors and sales each newsletter brings.
Track ads on platforms that do not tag links automatically.
Put a QR code on flyers, posters, packaging or event slides and measure the scans.
Give each partner their own utm_content value to compare their results.
tutorial: Paste the page you want people to visit in Website URL. If you leave out https://, it is added for you.
Tap a preset like Email newsletter or Instagram bio to fill in source and medium, or type them yourself.
Type a campaign name such as spring_sale or black_friday_2026. Spaces are replaced with underscores by default.
Campaign ID is used by some tools to join cost data. Term is for paid keywords. Content tells apart two links in the same post or email, like header_button and footer_link.
Your campaign URL shows the finished link with the tag values highlighted. Read any warning below it.
Press Copy URL, Open to test to check the page loads, or Download QR (PNG) for printed material.
features: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, LinkedIn, YouTube, WhatsApp, Telegram, email, ads, print, affiliate and SMS.
Optional lower case and your choice of underscore, hyphen, %20 or + for spaces.
Existing parameters and #anchors are preserved; old utm_ values are replaced.
A scannable QR code of the tagged link, ready to download.
Your last 10 copied links, stored only on your device.
Handles domain names and values in any language, encoded correctly.

example.title: Worked example: a newsletter link
example.text: Enter example.com/shop, tap Email newsletter (source newsletter, medium email) and type Spring Sale 2026 as the campaign. The link becomes https://example.com/shop?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=spring_sale_2026. Copy it into your newsletter. In your analytics tool, visits from it now appear under newsletter / email with the campaign spring_sale_2026.

tips: Agree on a short list of source and medium names with your team and always use the same spelling.
Use utm_content to compare two links or buttons in the same email or post.
Never tag links between pages of your own website; it overwrites the original source of the visit.
Long tagged links look messy in posts; a link shortener can hide them, and the tags still work.
Test the QR code with your phone before printing.
problems: Visits do not show the campaign
Make sure the tags are before any # in the link and that the page actually has your analytics code.
The same source appears twice in reports
Different spellings or capital letters were used, for example Facebook and facebook. Keep Make values lower case ticked.
It says the address does not look right
Use a normal web address with a domain, like https://example.com/page.
The link is too long for a QR code. Remove extra parameters or use a shorter page address.
